title: Signal and Noise
reflection: Notice one kind of static in your day, chatter, mood, loop or spike, and lower the floor a little, without fighting it.

questions.q: What is mental noise, according to Conversation 3.4?
o: Unwanted activity that hides a signal that is always there, like static on a radio.
A sign that the mind is failing to receive anything, so that the signal itself has been lost.
A fault of character, which a person is able to remove by simply trying a little harder.
A particular kind of thought, which only a few people ever have and most people never meet.
questions.e: The signal, whether the world, a quiet intuition or the simple sense of presence, is always there. Mental noise masks it. You are not failing to receive: the signal is buried.
questions.c: Noise hides a signal that is always there

questions.q: Two people hear the same quiet piece of music. One is rested, the other sleepless and overstimulated. What does Conversation 3.4 say?
o: The same signal, more noise: neither mind is better, one is simply in a quieter room.
The sleepless person hears a different piece, since the signal itself has changed.
The rested person is the better listener, since clarity is a matter of character.
Neither can hear it, since a quiet signal is always lost beneath any noise floor.
questions.e: Clarity is the ratio of signal to noise. A rested, quiet mind is a clear radio; a sleepless, overstimulated mind is a staticky one. The same signal, more noise.

questions.q: What is a noise floor, in Conversation 3.4?
o: The level of hiss below which quiet signals cannot be heard, as a whisper is lost in traffic.
The lowest point that a mood can reach, below which a person cannot sink any further.
The quietest hour of the night, when most people are asleep and the mind is at rest.
The surface of the body, through which every outside signal has to pass on its way in.
questions.e: Every system has a noise floor. When the floor is high, the subtlest goods, stillness and a calm steadiness, fall below it and cannot be heard.
questions.c: A high noise floor buries the subtlest goods

questions.q: A woman has a low, persistent unease that has no clear cause. Which kind of static is this, in Conversation 3.4?
o: A background mood: low persistent unease or sadness running under everything else.
Random chatter: scattered pointless thoughts that come and go in no order.
A stuck loop: an obsessive thought that repeats itself again and again.
A sudden spike: an intrusive memory or a jolt that arrives without warning.
questions.e: The four kinds of static are random chatter, a background mood, a stuck loop and sudden spikes. All are normal by-products of a busy mind; the trouble is only that, untrained, they run nonstop and keep the floor high.
questions.c: Persistent low unease is a background mood

questions.q: “Patañjali’s list of the obstacles of a scattered mind treats them as sins to be confessed.”
questions.e: Patañjali listed them as obstacles to understand, not sins: a scattered mind, pain, low spirits, a restless body and ragged breathing. The list closely matches today’s picture of anxiety and depression, and gives a reason for compassion and not for shame.
questions.c: The obstacles are to be understood, not confessed

questions.q: What are the three deep tilts of Conversation 3.4?
o: A sense of not enough, a sense of separation and a pull to repeat, in the instrument and not in you.
A habit of anger, a habit of fear and a habit of pride, which every person carries from birth.
A tilt of the body, a tilt of the breath and a tilt of the mind, which set the noise floor.
A pull toward the past, a pull toward the future and a pull toward other people.
questions.e: These are the three malas. Like a faint blue tint on every photo, the bias is in the instrument and not in you, and can be recalibrated.
questions.c: Not enough, separation, pull to repeat: biases in the instrument

questions.q: “Each ache is the faint signal of what it hides: you feel not enough only against a dim sense of fullness.”
questions.e: You feel not enough only against a dim sense of fullness, separate only against a dim unity, and trapped only against a dim freedom. The ache points to what it hides.
questions.c: Each ache is the faint signal of what it hides

questions.q: A man tries to fight his racing thoughts by forcing them quiet, and they grow louder. What does Conversation 3.4 suggest?
o: Lower the floor: simpler input, a settled body and one steady wholesome thing to rest on.
Try still harder, since the noise is certain to give way before enough effort.
Turn up the volume of the signal, so that it can be heard above the noise.
Ignore the noise completely and carry on, since nothing at all can lower it.
questions.e: Fighting static by trying harder is like turning up the volume: louder static. Lower the floor instead, with simpler input, a settled body, clean living and one steady wholesome thing such as the breath, a sacred word or a loved image.
questions.c: Lower the floor, do not fight the noise

questions.q: A teacher wants to quiet a noisy classroom without raising her voice. Which idea from Conversation 3.4 fits?
o: Lower the floor: less input, a settled rhythm and one steady thing to rest on.
Speak above the noise, since a louder signal is the only way to be heard by all of them.
Wait for the noise to pass by itself, since a noise floor cannot be changed by anyone at all.
Single out the loudest pupils, since they alone are the cause of the whole of the high floor.
questions.e: Practice does not manufacture peace: it lowers the floor so that what was always broadcasting can be heard. The same applies to a room, with simpler input and a steady rhythm.
questions.c: Quiet a room by lowering the floor, not raising the volume

questions.q: A man says, “I only feel peace when I get rid of every thought.” How does Conversation 3.4 reply?
o: Peace is heard and not made: the calm watcher and the gaps between thoughts were always there.
Peace comes only from silencing every single thought, so he should keep up the effort.
Peace is a mood, which comes and goes at random and cannot be influenced by him at all.
Peace is for a few people only, so he should not expect it in an ordinary and busy life.
questions.e: Practice lowers the floor so that what was always broadcasting, the gaps between thoughts and the calm watcher underneath, can be heard. Peace is uncovered, not produced.
